After 1956, the Sino-Soviet alliance began to break down.
Mao had defended Stalin when Khrushchev criticized him in 1956 and treated the new Soviet leader as a superficial upstart, accusing him of having lost his revolutionary edge.
For his part, Khrushchev, disturbed by Mao's glib attitude toward nuclear war, referred to the Chinese leader as a "lunatic on a throne".
After this, Khrushchev made many desperate attempts to reconstitute the Sino-Soviet alliance, but Mao considered it useless and denied any proposal.
The Chinese-Soviet animosity spilled out in an intra-communist propaganda war.
the Soviets focused on a bitter rivalry with Mao's China for leadership of the global communist movement.
During the Sino-Soviet split, "spy wars" also occurred between the USSR and PRC.
As a result of the Sino-Soviet split, tensions along the Chinese-Soviet border reached their peak in 1969, when the Soviet planned to launch a large-scale nuclear strike against China.

United States President Richard Nixon intervened, and decided to use the conflict to shift the balance of power towards the West in the Cold War through a policy of rapproachment with China, which began with his 1972 visit to China and culminated in 1979 with the signing of the Joint Communique on the Establishment of Diplomatic Relations by President Carter and Chinese Communist Party leader Deng Xiaoping.

Nixon used rapprochement (the re-establishment of cordial relations) to isolate the Soviet Union.
Detente refers to the general easing of tensions between the US and USSR.
Rollback was a strategy to overthrow existing communist regimes.
Nixon sought to engage China, not isolate it.
Appeasement is the policy of making concessions to avoid conflict.
De-Stalinization was Khrushchev's policy of removing Stalin's influence.

mini_games.question: The strategic pivot toward China culminated in 1979 with the signing of the ____.

options.feedback: The Helsinki Accords were an agreement between the West and the Soviet Union.

The Warsaw Pact was a Soviet-led military alliance.
The Truman Doctrine was the early US policy of containment.
The Marshall Plan was a US economic aid program for Western Europe.
The INF Treaty was a 1987 agreement to eliminate certain nuclear missiles.
